newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PdVSA aims at 50 pct stake in Mobil refinery.
newsitem.headline: PdVSA aims at 50 pct stake in Mobil refinery.

text.p: Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) subsidiary Lagoven plans to take a 50 percent stake in Mobil Oil Corporation's 170,000 barrels per day refinery in Chalmette Louisiana, Lagoven said.
"Our final intention is that each of the companies take a fifty percent share in the refinery," Lagoven President Julius Trinkunas told reporters.
However, Trinkunas declined to comment on how much Lagoven would pay for the refinery.
"We would prefer not to discuss that in public," he said.
The refinery stake forms part of a larger $2.3 billion memorandum of understanding signed between the two companies on Tuesday.

About 100,000 bpd of extra heavy crude from the Cerro Negro area of Venezuela's Orinocco Tar Belt will be upgraded and sold under the deal which forms one of several designed to take advantage of Venezuela's huge heavy crude reserves.
PdVSA affiliate Corpoven recently signed a $3.5 billion deal with Atlantic Richfield Co to upgrade and market 197,000 bpd of crude from the Tar Belt.
Mobil also recently started exploration work for light and medium crudes in Western Venezuela under a profit-sharing agreement in partnership with Germany's Veba Oel and Japan's Nippon Oil Co Ltd.
